# T4.1 · Reactive 3D avatar (revised)

**Status:** parked, unscheduled. Not to be started until Tiers 0–3 are closed.
**Revision:** v2 — skin is generated by AI, skeleton is prebuilt. Supersedes the
original "fixed base mesh + portrait as texture" draft.

---

## Core principle

**The skeleton is authored once. The skin is generated every time.**

Nothing about the character's visual identity is hand-made. The only thing that is
hand-made is invisible: the mesh topology, the UV seams, the contact points and the
blendshapes — all of which must be fixed *before* a texture is applied, and none of
which require an artist.

Three independent layers:

| Layer | Who makes it | Changes per character? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Body library (mesh, UVs, zones, blendshapes) | authored once, ships with the app | no |
| Skin (albedo + metallic-roughness) | AI | yes, every character |
| Emotion + mouth + click reactions | app code, procedural | no |

---

## Layer 1 — Body library (prebuilt, shipped)

A small set of prebuilt busts bundled with the app: **8–12 silhouettes**
(varied build, age range, hair mass, head shape), covering the range a chat
character needs.

Requirements each bust must satisfy *before* it enters the library:

- **UV unwrapped, no overlapping or mirrored islands.** UltraTex bakes onto UVs; bad
  UVs produce smeared textures. This is the single hardest technical requirement.
- **Named zones as vertex groups**, e.g.
  `head`, `cheek.L`, `cheek.R`, `hair`, `neck`, `chest`, `shoulder.L`, `shoulder.R`,
  `hand.L`, `hand.R`, `lap`, `held`.
- **Blendshapes** for `neutral, warm, amused, cold, tense, angry, sad, afraid,
  surprised` plus `jaw_open`, `blink.L`, `blink.R`, `brow_raise`, `brow_furrow`.
- **Poly budget** under ~150k faces (keeps the bake fast and the WebView2 viewport
  cheap on integrated GPUs).
- **Source: MakeHuman.** Exported MakeHuman meshes are CC0 (the app itself is AGPL,
  the output is not), it has a rigged base mesh and expression morphs, and its sliders
  mean the body library is built by dragging dials — no sculpting, no art skill.
  Authoring the extra zones/blendshapes is mechanical Blender work, roughly an
  afternoon per bust, and it happens exactly once for the whole product.

**Contact points are defined here, not later.** This is the part that must be
finished before any texture is ever applied: a zone that doesn't exist on the base
mesh cannot be clicked, and a zone cannot be added after hundreds of textured assets
depend on the old topology.

Each zone maps to one bracketed context template, held in app config so wording is
tunable without a rebuild:

| Zone | Injected on click |
| --- | --- |
| `hand.L` / `hand.R` | `[User takes the character's hand]` |
| `cheek.L` / `cheek.R` | `[User touches the character's cheek]` |
| `hair` | `[User brushes a strand of hair from the character's face]` |
| `chest` | `[User rests a hand on the character's chest]` |
| `shoulder.L` / `shoulder.R` | `[User touches the character's shoulder]` |
| `held` | `[User gestures toward what the character is holding]` |

Rules: rate-limited (one injection per few seconds), never mutates chat or game
state by itself, and the model is never told it has an avatar — it only ever
receives the bracketed line as normal context.

---

## Layer 2 — Skin (AI-generated)

**Reference portrait → textured mesh.** The pipeline is:

```
character appearance
        │
        ▼
[1] reference portrait   ← existing image generator (sd.cpp, already in app)
        │
        ▼
[2] texture bake         ← UltraTex: mesh + 1 reference image → albedo + MR maps
        │
        ▼
[3] textured .glb        → Documents\Howl Chat\Avatars\<character>\
```

**Step 1 — reference portrait.** Generated with the app's existing image pipeline,
using a fixed prompt scaffold so the bake comes out clean:

```
<character appearance>, front view, facing camera, symmetrical, even neutral
lighting, plain light grey background, upper body, no text, no watermark
```

Fixed suffix is not optional. UltraTex paints scene lighting into the albedo and
aligns the reference to its front camera, so a dramatic-lit or side-turned portrait
bakes badly. Users can override the portrait, but the default scaffold produces the
best result.

**Step 2 — texture bake.** UltraTex (SIGGRAPH Asia 2026, MIT code, weights public):
- Input: untextured mesh + one reference image.
- Process: renders the mesh from six camera angles, paints all six at once with
  FLUX.2 Klein for cross-view consistency, bakes back onto the mesh UVs.
- Output: albedo + metallic-roughness, baked at up to 2K.
- VRAM: **~6.8GB peak** on the low-VRAM GGUF (Q4) workflow — fits an 8GB card.
  Standard 6-view workflow wants 12–16GB, or 8–12GB at 1024px. Use the GGUF workflow.
- Back of the mesh is *guessed* by the model. For a front-facing chat avatar this is
  invisible; it only matters if the character is ever turned around.

**Step 3 — storage.** One `.glb` plus maps per character under the per-character
avatar folder. Regenerating is a manual, explicit action.

### Integration reality (the honest part)

UltraTex is a ComfyUI/Python pipeline. HOWL Chat is Go + Wails with cgo forbidden
and no embedded Python runtime, so it **cannot** ship inside the binary. Integration
is therefore an *optional external tool*, in the same shape as the existing
stable-diffusion server the app already talks to over HTTP:

- Settings gets a "3D texturing server" URL (default `http://127.0.0.1:8188`).
- The app POSTs a pinned workflow JSON with the mesh path and reference image, then
  polls for the result.
- Upstream provides a one-click Windows installer plus three ready-made workflows.
- If the endpoint is unreachable, the app does not fail — it drops to Tier B below.

### VRAM discipline

Same lock as the image generator: chat model unloads first if both won't fit, with
the usual confirm dialog; texturing model unloads immediately after the bake.
Generation is one-time per character — playback never touches the 3D pipeline again.

---

## Graceful ladder (the important part)

The avatar must never be an all-or-nothing feature, because the user is not an
artist and should not have to install anything to get a character that looks like
themselves.

| Tier | Requires | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A** | nothing (today) | card portrait, or character image set (T2.5) |
| **B** | 3D only, no extra tools | prebuilt bust wearing the portrait, planar-projected onto the front UV island, mirrored and darkened for the back with a seam blend. Front looks right, sides are flat. Costs nothing extra — the app already has UVs and the portrait. |
| **C** | + ComfyUI & UltraTex | full PBR bake, correct from every angle, AI art |
| **D** | + TripoSR-class | generated head or bust geometry instead of a library body — later, optional |

Tier B is app-side only and needs no new dependencies. It is the default 3D
experience, so every user gets a living avatar; Tier C is the upgrade for users who
already run ComfyUI. Any failure at C falls back to B without a dialog.

Final fallback chain, never a blank panel: **avatar → image set → initial on dark blue.**

---

## Layer 3 — Emotion, mouth, idle

- **Emotion is an app-owned enum**, fixed:
  `neutral, warm, amused, cold, tense, angry, sad, afraid, surprised`.
  Source order: optional trailing model tag (`[mood: amused]`, validated, dropped if
  outside the enum) → deterministic keyword/sentiment scan of the reply.
  Blend weights over 0.3–0.6s, with hysteresis and a ~1.5s minimum hold so it cannot
  flicker mid-sentence.
- **Mouth** is driven by the TTS audio amplitude envelope (real speech → real mouth).
  Fallback with TTS off: token rhythm with punctuation-weighted pauses.
  Text rendering never waits on the face.
- **Idle life:** breathing, blink, slight head drift, all procedural loops. No mocap,
  no animation clips, no neural rendering.

---

## Performance constraints (8GB and integrated GPUs)

- WebGL compositing shares the GPU with llama.cpp. Cap the viewport at **30fps**,
  pause rendering while tokens are generating, render on demand when idle.
- **Requirement:** measure tokens/s with the viewport on vs off before shipping. If
  the cost is more than a small fraction, the avatar pauses during generation by
  default rather than being removed.
- If WebView2/WebGL2 is unavailable, fall straight through to images, silently.

---

## Licensing flag

- UltraTex code and both ComfyUI node packs: **MIT**.
- FLUX.2 Klein base weights: **non-commercial** (Black Forest Labs states it claims
  no ownership of outputs).
- Consequence: the Tier C bake path is fine for personal use but is *not* safe to
  present as a commercial feature until a commercially licensed base model is
  substituted. Tier B uses only the app's own image generator and carries no such
  caveat. Not legal advice — read the terms before selling anything.

## Open questions (must be answered before this stage is scoped)

1. UltraTex GGUF at 1024 on an 8GB card: actual bake time and seam quality on a bust
   (not a game prop). Reported first run 496s including model load; later runs faster.
2. Does a MakeHuman-derived bust survive UltraTex's UV requirements without manual
   island cleanup?
3. Token-speed cost of the live viewport — measure, don't assume.
4. Whether the ComfyUI dependency is acceptable at all, or whether Tier B alone is
   the shipped feature and Tier C stays a power-user path.

**Not verified:** every number above comes from third-party reporting on other
hardware. None of it has been measured on this machine.
